name: Drought
value: Sudan near record-poor harvest; no famine
summary: El Niño drought covers about half of Sudan, with harvests seen near record-poor; no major exporter's harvest failure
state: An IPC alert of 12 Oct said an El Niño-induced drought affects roughly half of Sudan, and the IRC said on 13 Oct that harvests there are expected to be near record-poor after delayed rains devastated planting in North Darfur. In South Africa, commentary on 2 Nov said El Niño threatens the coming crop but ample maize stocks cushion the blow (Daily Maverick). Searches on 23 Nov found no drought-driven famine declaration and no harvest failure at a major exporter, so severe drought in crop regions keeps Watch.
for_you: Drought in Sudan and the El Niño risk to southern African crops mainly affect local food supply and prices. Global grain markets are not currently showing a major exporter's harvest failure.
rubric_hit: Severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan, El Niño) = Watch; no exporter harvest failure

sources.title: IRC — War and El Niño-driven drought deplete food stocks, pushing Sudan further towards famine
Daily Maverick — El Niño threatens SA's crops but ample maize stocks cushion the blow

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
